title: "Lebanon: malapportionment and seat-allocation counterfactuals"
author: "Elyse St Sauver, Peyton Howard"

output: html_document

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

# One helper so every table in the document looks the same.
ktab <- function(x, caption, col.names = NA, digits = 2, ...) {
  kbl(x, caption = caption, col.names = col.names, digits = digits,
      row.names = FALSE, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), ...) |>
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                  full_width = FALSE, position = "left")
}

# LaTeX twin of ktab, for the results section. It PRINTS the table source so a subsection
# can be run on its own and the result pasted straight into a LaTeX document; nothing is
# written to disk and no other chunk has to be run first.
#
# Your preamble needs: booktabs, array (bold columns), graphicx (rotated headers and
# \resizebox), and lscape or pdflscape (the wide tables). Captions carry a \label rather
# than a hard-coded number, so LaTeX numbers them by position in your document.
#
#   fit       upright, but squeezed to \linewidth: tight padding and \resizebox. For the
#             two 16-column tables, which cannot fit a portrait page at full size.
#   wide      as `fit`, and additionally turned sideways with rotated headers. Bigger
#             type, at the cost of a landscape page - set wide = TRUE if you prefer that.
#   bold_row  / bold_col   emphasise a summary row / column
#   bold_cells  logical matrix over the body columns 2..ncol(x), bolding individual
#               entries. Used to mark which cells actually hold a seat.
#   pack      named vector of group sizes, printed as subheadings instead of a label column
#   header    named vector of column-group widths, printed as a spanning row above the column
#             names, so a family of columns is labelled once. Must sum to ncol(x). Not
#             compatible with `wide`, which rotates the same row.
#   note      text set under the table as "Note: ...". LaTeX is passed through, so \ref works.
#             Needs threeparttable in the preamble.
ltab <- function(x, caption, label, col.names = NA, digits = 2, fit = FALSE,
                 wide = FALSE, align = NULL, bold_row = NULL, bold_col = NULL,
                 bold_cells = NULL, pack = NULL, header = NULL, note = NULL) {
  if (is.null(align)) align <- paste0("l", strrep("r", ncol(x) - 1))
  squeeze <- fit || wide
  out <- kbl(x, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "", escape = TRUE,
             caption = caption, label = label, col.names = col.names, digits = digits,
             row.names = FALSE, align = align,
             format.args = list(big.mark = ",")) |>
    kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position", if (squeeze) "scale_down"))
  if (!is.null(bold_cells)) {
    # column_spec takes a logical vector down the column, so apply it column by column.
    stopifnot(nrow(bold_cells) == nrow(x), ncol(bold_cells) == ncol(x) - 1L)
    for (j in seq_len(ncol(bold_cells)))
      out <- column_spec(out, j + 1L, bold = bold_cells[, j])
  }
  # `header` is a spanning row above the column names, as a named vector of group widths -
  # e.g. c(" " = 3, "Gallagher" = 3, "Loosemore-Hanby" = 2) - so a family of columns can be
  # labelled once instead of repeating the name in every heading. It must total ncol(x).
  # Applied before the row_spec calls below, since row 0 would otherwise be ambiguous: do not
  # combine `header` with `wide`, which rotates row 0.
  if (!is.null(header)) {
    stopifnot(sum(header) == ncol(x), is.null(wide) || !wide)
    out <- add_header_above(out, header)
  }
  if (!is.null(bold_row)) out <- row_spec(out, bold_row, bold = TRUE)
  if (!is.null(bold_col)) out <- column_spec(out, bold_col, bold = TRUE)
  if (!is.null(pack))     out <- pack_rows(out, index = pack)
  if (wide) out <- row_spec(out, 0, angle = 45)
  if (!is.null(note))
    out <- footnote(out, general = note, general_title = "Note:", footnote_as_chunk = TRUE,
                    threeparttable = TRUE, escape = FALSE)
  if (squeeze) {
    # After the FIRST \centering - not after \begin{table}, which would land between it
    # and its [!h] placement option and leave "[!h]" to be typeset as text.
    out <- sub("\\centering", "\\centering\n\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{3pt}",
               out, fixed = TRUE)
  }
  if (wide) out <- landscape(out)
  cat(out, "\n")
  invisible(out)
}
```

# 1. What this computes
The Malapportionment Indices

Lebanon apportions 128 parliamentary seats on two dimensions at once. Seats are assigned
to 15 electoral districts, and within each district to specific confessions - the seat is
not "a seat for Bcharre", it is "the Maronite seat for Bcharre". So there are three
questions to ask, not one:

1. **Geographic.** Do the 15 districts hold seats in proportion to their voters?
2. **Confessional.** Do the confessions hold seats in proportion to their voters?
3. **District x faith.** Does each confession hold seats in each district in proportion to
   its voters there?

Two indices are reported throughout. The first is Samuels and Snyder's index of
malapportionment scaled by the number of seats n, abbreviated SLH in the text and named in full in table headings where
there is room for it:

$$\text{SLH} = \frac{n}{2}\sum_i \left| s_i - v_i \right|$$

where $s_i$ is unit $i$'s share of seats and $v_i$ its share of registered voters, both in
percent. SLH is 0 under exact proportionality. It reads as the percentage of seats that
would have to change hands to reach proportionality, so multiplying by n turns it into a
count of seats.

The second is the **Gallagher least-squares index**, which squares the deviations rather
than taking absolute values:

$$\text{Gallagher} = \sqrt{\tfrac{1}{2}\sum_i \left( s_i - v_i \right)^2}$$

The two answer different questions. SLH asks *how many seats are in the wrong place*, which
is the natural way to describe a status quo. Gallagher asks *how badly are they in the wrong
place*, because a squared term punishes one unit being far off more than several being
slightly off. That difference is irrelevant when describing a single seat table but decisive
when ranking reforms - so the descriptive tables lead with SLH, while the seat-table
optimisation in 5.5 is scored on Gallagher.

The three levels are nested: the geographic and confessional units are both aggregations of
the district x faith cell. **For SLH**, aggregating lets positive and negative deviations
cancel, so the cell index can never be smaller than either of the other two. The interesting
quantity is the gap - a confession can hold exactly its national share of seats and still
hold them in the wrong districts, and only the cell index sees that.

That cross-share comparability does not hold for Gallagher, and Table 1 shows it failing. Confessional
Gallagher (10.63) is nearly double the cell figure (5.36), the opposite of the SLH ordering.
Squaring is the reason: one confession short by 8.6 points nationally contributes 8.6² = 74
to the sum, but the same shortfall spread over fifteen districts as roughly 0.6 points each
contributes only about 5. Absolute values do not care how a deviation is distributed;
squares punish concentration heavily. So a Gallagher figure is only ever comparable with
another Gallagher figure computed over the *same* units - never across levels.

**On the denominator.** These are registration counts, not residents and not votes cast.
Lebanese register in their ancestral village rather than where they live, and there has
been no census since 1932, so no population denominator exists to check them against.
What is measured here is apportionment relative to the electoral roll - which is the thing
the law itself operates on.

# 2. Data

`seats.csv` is the statutory allocation, one row per qada with a column per confession.
It is grouped up to the 15 electoral districts here. The allocation is identical in 2018,
2022 and 2026, so it is not year-specific - the 2022 rows are used because that is the
year the voter roll covers.

`voters_by_district_sect_long.csv` is the 2022 register (3,967,507 registrants) at minor
district x sect, extracted from the Ministry of Interior's final release. It is aggregated
up to the same 15 districts. The file omits combinations with no registrants rather than
storing a zero, so the grid is completed explicitly.

```{r data}
FAITH <- c(sunni             = "Sunni",
           shia              = "Shia",
           druze             = "Druze",
           alawite           = "Alawite",
           maronite          = "Maronite",
           greek_catholic    = "Greek Catholic",
           greek_orthodox    = "Greek Orthodox",
           evangelical       = "Protestant",            # voter file's label
           armenian_catholic = "Armenian Catholic",
           armenian_orthodox = "Armenian Orthodox",
           minorities        = "Christian Minorities")  # voter file's label

# voter-file district name -> the slug used in seats.csv
DISTRICT <- c("Beirut I"          = "beirut_1", "Beirut II"        = "beirut_2",
              "Bekaa I"           = "bekaa_1",  "Bekaa II"         = "bekaa_2",
              "Bekaa III"         = "bekaa_3",
              "Mount Lebanon I"   = "mt_leb_1", "Mount Lebanon II" = "mt_leb_2",
              "Mount Lebanon III" = "mt_leb_3", "Mount Lebanon IV" = "mt_leb_4",
              "North I"           = "n_leb_1",  "North II"         = "n_leb_2",
              "North III"         = "n_leb_3",
              "South I"           = "s_leb_1",  "South II"         = "s_leb_2",
              "South III"         = "s_leb_3")

# Slug -> printable district name, and a short form for table headers. The full names run
# to "Mount Lebanon III", far too wide for a 16-column table; abbreviating them is what
# lets those tables be set upright rather than sideways.
DNAME <- setNames(names(DISTRICT), unname(DISTRICT))
DABBR <- setNames(names(DISTRICT) |>
                    str_replace("^Beirut ", "Bei ") |>
                    str_replace("^Bekaa ", "Bek ") |>
                    str_replace("^Mount Lebanon ", "ML ") |>
                    str_replace("^North ", "N ") |>
                    str_replace("^South ", "S "),
                  unname(DISTRICT))

# Seats: one row per district x faith. seats.csv carries a qada total in a column already
# called `seats`, so only the per-confession columns are taken forward.
seats_dc <- read.csv("seats.csv") |>
  filter(year == 2022) |>
  select(district, all_of(names(FAITH))) |>
  pivot_longer(-district, names_to = "faith", values_to = "seats") |>
  mutate(faith = unname(FAITH[faith])) |>
  summarise(seats = sum(seats), .by = c(district, faith))

# Voters: same grain. `Other` has registrants but holds no seat of any kind, so it stays
# in with seats = 0 rather than being dropped from the denominator.
vot_dc <- read.csv("data/population - registered voters/voters_by_district_sect_long.csv",
                   fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM") |>
  mutate(district = unname(DISTRICT[major_district]), faith = sect_en) |>
  summarise(voters = sum(registered_total), residents = sum(registered_resident),
            .by = c(district, faith))

# The full 15 x 12 grid. The voter file stores no row for a district-faith pair with no
# registrants, and seats_dc carries no row for `Other`, so both sides are filled with 0.
dc <- expand_grid(district = unname(DISTRICT), faith = sort(unique(vot_dc$faith))) |>
  left_join(seats_dc, by = c("district", "faith")) |>
  left_join(vot_dc,   by = c("district", "faith")) |>
  mutate(across(c(seats, voters, residents), \(x) replace_na(x, 0))) |>
  mutate(dist_name = names(DISTRICT)[match(district, DISTRICT)], .after = district)

# Nothing was lost or invented in the reshaping.
stopifnot(
  nrow(dc) == 15 * 12,
  sum(dc$seats)  == 128,
  sum(dc$voters) == sum(read.csv(
    "data/population - registered voters/voters_by_district_sect_long.csv",
    fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")$registered_total),
  !any(is.na(dc)))

cat(sprintf("%d district x faith cells | %d seats | %s registrants | %d cells hold a seat\n",
            nrow(dc), sum(dc$seats), format(sum(dc$voters), big.mark = ","),
            sum(dc$seats > 0)))
```

# 3. Computing the index

```{r index}
# SLH over a set of units. `s` and `v` are counts, not shares; they are normalized here so
# that a unit absent from one side simply contributes its full share on the other.
mal <- function(s, v) sum(abs(100 * s / sum(s) - 100 * v / sum(v))) / 2

# Collapse the cell table to a level and score it. `by` is the grouping - no grouping at
# all (`NULL`) would be a single unit and a score of 0, so every call names at least one.
score <- function(data, by, voters = voters) {
  g <- summarise(data, s = sum(seats), v = sum({{ voters }}), .by = all_of(by))
  mal(g$s, g$v)
}

# Gallagher's least-squares index, over the same units. It squares the deviations instead
# of taking absolute values, so unlike SLH it registers HOW far a unit is from its share,
# not just that it is off. That distinction decides which index can rank a reform: see
# the note under Table 1.
gallagher <- function(s, v) sqrt(sum((100 * s / sum(s) - 100 * v / sum(v))^2) / 2)
score_g <- function(data, by, voters = voters) {
  g <- summarise(data, s = sum(seats), v = sum({{ voters }}), .by = all_of(by))
  gallagher(g$s, g$v)
}

# --- the same cells as a plain vector ------------------------------------------
# `dc` from section 2 is already the full district x confession grid, so fixing its row
# order turns any seat table into a vector of 180 counts. Section 5 perturbs that vector
# and scores it with `indices()` below, so both live here rather than in whichever section happened to need them first.
cells    <- dc |> arrange(district, faith)
key180   <- paste(cells$district, cells$faith, sep = "|")
faiths12 <- sort(unique(cells$faith))
S0 <- cells$seats
V0 <- cells$voters

dmap <- match(cells$district, unname(DISTRICT))
fmap <- match(cells$faith, faiths12)
agg  <- function(x, m, k) as.vector(tapply(x, factor(m, levels = seq_len(k)), sum,
                                           default = 0))
vp  <- 100 * V0 / sum(V0)
vpd <- 100 * agg(V0, dmap, 15) / sum(V0)
vpf <- 100 * agg(V0, fmap, 12) / sum(V0)

# Both indices at all three levels, for any seat vector.
indices <- function(S) {
  Sd <- agg(S, dmap, 15); Sf <- agg(S, fmap, 12); T <- sum(S)
  c(mal_geo  = sum(abs(100*Sd/T - vpd))/2,
    mal_conf = sum(abs(100*Sf/T - vpf))/2,
    mal_cell = sum(abs(100*S /T - vp ))/2,
    gal_cell = sqrt(sum((100*S /T - vp )^2)/2),
    gal_geo  = sqrt(sum((100*Sd/T - vpd)^2)/2),
    gal_conf = sqrt(sum((100*Sf/T - vpf)^2)/2))
}
base_ix <- indices(S0)

# The vector route and the data-frame route must agree.
stopifnot(sum(S0) == 128,
          all.equal(unname(base_ix[1:3]),
                    c(score(dc, "district"), score(dc, "faith"),
                      score(dc, c("district", "faith"))), tolerance = 1e-8))
```

# 4. Computing SLH and Gallagher Scores

```{r scores}
levels_ <- list(Geographic          = "district",
                Confessional        = "faith",
                `District x faith`  = c("district", "faith"))

scores <- tibble(
  level = names(levels_),
  unit  = c("15 electoral districts", "12 confessions", "15 x 12 cells"),
  n     = c(15, 12, 180),
  mal   = map_dbl(levels_, \(b) score(dc, b)),
  mal_r = map_dbl(levels_, \(b) score(dc, b, residents)),
  gal   = map_dbl(levels_, \(b) score_g(dc, b))) |>
  mutate(seats = mal / 100 * 128)

# Aggregation can only let deviations cancel, so the cell index bounds the other two.
# This is asserted for SLH only: Gallagher is NOT monotone under refinement, and in fact
# runs the other way here - see the note above Table 1.
stopifnot(scores$mal[1] <= scores$mal[3] + 1e-9,
          scores$mal[2] <= scores$mal[3] + 1e-9,
          scores$gal[2] >  scores$gal[3])          # the non-monotonicity, pinned down

ktab(scores |> relocate(seats, .after = gal),
     caption = "Table 1. Malapportionment of the 128 seats, 2022 register.",
     col.names = c("Level", "Unit", "Units", "SLH", "SLH, residents only",
                   "Gallagher", "Seats misallocated"),
     digits = c(0, 0, 0, 2, 2, 3, 1))
```

The two one-dimensional indices are each substantially smaller than the joint one. The gap
between the confessional index and the cell index is the "right total, wrong place"
problem: it is the misallocation that survives even after every confession has been given
its correct national number of seats.

Because Gallagher squares, it is dominated by the worst-placed units rather than spread
evenly over all of them, so the index is best read alongside its largest contributors.

```{r gal-contrib}
contributors <- function(by, label) {
  g  <- summarise(dc, s = sum(seats), v = sum(voters), .by = all_of(by))
  d  <- 100 * g$s / sum(g$s) - 100 * g$v / sum(g$v)
  tibble(level = label, unit = apply(g[by], 1, paste, collapse = " / "),
         deviation = d, squared = d^2) |>
    mutate(share = 100 * squared / sum(squared)) |> slice_max(squared, n = 3)
}

ktab(bind_rows(contributors("faith", "Confessional"),
               contributors("district", "Geographic")),
     caption = paste0("Table 2. The three largest contributors to each Gallagher index. ",
                      "Deviation is seat share minus voter share, in percentage points."),
     col.names = c("Level", "Unit", "Deviation (pp)", "Squared", "% of the index"),
     digits = c(0, 0, 2, 1, 1))
```

Three confessions - Sunni, Shia and Maronite - account for 88% of the confessional index
between them. The geographic index is less concentrated: its top three units make up 63%.

## 4.1. Geographic

`entitled` is the seat count a district would hold under exact proportionality, and
`surplus` is what it actually holds minus that. Voters per seat is the same fact read
directly: the national figure is 3,967,507 / 128, and a district below it is
over-represented, because each of its voters counts for more in returning a member.

```{r geographic}
geo <- dc |>
  summarise(voters = sum(voters), seats = sum(seats), .by = c(district, dist_name)) |>
  mutate(voter_pct = 100 * voters / sum(voters),
         seat_pct  = 100 * seats  / sum(seats),
         per_seat  = voters / seats,
         entitled  = 128 * voters / sum(voters),
         surplus   = seats - entitled,
         advantage = seat_pct / voter_pct) |>
  arrange(per_seat)

ktab(select(geo, dist_name, district, voters, seats, per_seat, voter_pct, seat_pct,
            entitled, surplus, advantage),
     caption = paste0("Table 3. Geographic apportionment, most to least over-represented. ",
                      "SLH = ", sprintf("%.2f", score(dc, "district")), "."),
     col.names = c("District", "Slug", "Registered", "Seats", "Voters/seat", "Voter %",
                   "Seat %", "Entitled", "Surplus", "Advantage"),
     digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 2, 1, 1, 2))

cat(sprintf("National: %s registrants / 128 seats = %s voters per seat\n",
            format(sum(geo$voters), big.mark = ","),
            format(round(sum(geo$voters) / 128), big.mark = ",")))
cat(sprintf("Most to least over-represented: %.2f : 1 (%s vs %s)\n",
            max(geo$per_seat) / min(geo$per_seat),
            geo$dist_name[which.min(geo$per_seat)],
            geo$dist_name[which.max(geo$per_seat)]))
```

## 4.2 Confessional

```{r confessional}
con <- dc |>
  summarise(voters = sum(voters), seats = sum(seats), .by = faith) |>
  mutate(voter_pct = 100 * voters / sum(voters),
         seat_pct  = 100 * seats  / sum(seats),
         entitled  = 128 * voters / sum(voters),
         surplus   = seats - entitled,
         advantage = seat_pct / voter_pct) |>
  arrange(desc(surplus))

ktab(con,
     caption = paste0("Table 4. Confessional apportionment, most to least ",
                      "over-represented. SLH = ",
                      sprintf("%.2f", score(dc, "faith")), "."),
     col.names = c("Confession", "Registered", "Seats", "Voter %", "Seat %",
                   "Entitled", "Surplus", "Advantage"),
     digits = c(0, 0, 0, 2, 2, 1, 1, 2))
```

`Other` is 20,968 registrants with no seat of any kind - not an under-allocated
confession but an unrepresented one. It is kept in the denominator, which is why the
advantage column reads 0 rather than blank.

## 4.3 District x faith

Entitlement here is still 128 x the cell's share of the **national** roll, so these
surpluses are on the same scale as the two tables above and sum to zero across the grid.
Blank cells have neither seats nor registrants.

```{r cell-grid}
ABBR <- c(Sunni = "Sunni", Shia = "Shia", Druze = "Druze", Alawite = "Alaw",
          Maronite = "Maron", `Greek Catholic` = "GkCath", `Greek Orthodox` = "GkOrth",
          Protestant = "Prot", `Armenian Catholic` = "ArmCath",
          `Armenian Orthodox` = "ArmOrth", `Christian Minorities` = "ChrMin",
          Other = "Other")

cell <- dc |>
  mutate(entitled = 128 * voters / sum(voters),
         surplus  = seats - entitled)

grid <- cell |>
  mutate(faith = factor(unname(ABBR[faith]), levels = unname(ABBR)),
         surplus = if_else(seats == 0 & voters == 0, NA, surplus)) |>
  select(dist_name, faith, surplus) |>
  arrange(faith) |>                     # pivot_wider takes column order from the rows
  pivot_wider(names_from = faith, values_from = surplus) |>
  arrange(match(dist_name, names(DISTRICT)))

ktab(grid,
     caption = paste0("Table 5. Seats held minus seats entitled, by district and faith. ",
                      "Positive = over-represented. SLH = ",
                      sprintf("%.2f", score(dc, c("district", "faith"))), "."),
     col.names = c("District", unname(ABBR)),
     digits = 1) |>
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
```

```{r cell-extremes}
ktab(cell |>
       slice_max(abs(surplus), n = 15) |>
       mutate(per_seat = if_else(seats > 0, voters / seats, NA)) |>
       select(dist_name, faith, seats, voters, entitled, surplus, per_seat),
     caption = "Table 6. The 15 cells furthest from proportionality, either direction.",
     col.names = c("District", "Confession", "Seats", "Registered", "Entitled",
                   "Surplus", "Voters/seat"),
     digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 2, 0))

seatless <- filter(cell, seats == 0, voters > 0)
cat(sprintf("%d of %d cells have registrants but no seat: %s people, %.1f%% of the roll\n",
            nrow(seatless), nrow(cell), format(sum(seatless$voters), big.mark = ","),
            100 * sum(seatless$voters) / sum(cell$voters)))
```

# 5. Results

## 5.1 Voters per seat, confession by district

```{r vps-matrix, comment = ""}
vps_mat <- dc |>
  filter(faith != "Other") |>
  mutate(vps = if_else(seats > 0, voters / seats / 1000, NA_real_)) |>
  select(district, faith, vps) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = district, values_from = vps) |>
  arrange(faith)

row_avg <- dc |> filter(faith != "Other") |> summarise(v = sum(voters), s = sum(seats),
                                                       .by = faith) |>
  transmute(faith, `All districts` = v / s / 1000)
col_avg <- dc |> summarise(v = sum(voters), s = sum(seats), .by = district) |>
  transmute(district, avg = v / s / 1000)

vps_out <- vps_mat |> left_join(row_avg, by = "faith") |>
  bind_rows(col_avg |> pivot_wider(names_from = district, values_from = avg) |>
              mutate(faith = "Avg",
                     `All districts` = sum(dc$voters) / 128 / 1000))

ltab(vps_out,
     caption = paste0("Registered voters per seat, in thousands, by confession and ",
                      "electoral district. 2022 Data"),
     note = paste0("The national figure is ",
                   format(round(sum(dc$voters) / 128), big.mark = ","),
                   " registrants per seat (",
                   sprintf("%.1f", sum(dc$voters) / 128 / 1000), " in thousands). ",
                   "Districts are abbreviated Bei = Beirut, Bek = Bekaa, ML = Mount Lebanon, ",
                   "N = North, S = South. Where there is no representative for a given ",
                   "confession in a district, that value is left blank. The average number of ",
                   "registrants per representative seat by confession is reported in the ",
                   "rightmost column, and the average number of registrants per seat by ",
                   "district is reported in the last row."),
     label = "voters-per-seat",
     col.names = c("", DABBR[names(vps_mat)[-1]], "Avg"),
     digits = 1, fit = TRUE,
     bold_row = nrow(vps_out), bold_col = ncol(vps_out))
```

## 5.2 Malapportionment within each district

```{r mal-by-district, comment = ""}
by_district <- dc |>
  summarise(gal = gallagher(seats, voters), n_seats = sum(seats), .by = district) |>
  arrange(desc(gal)) |>
  transmute(district = DNAME[district], seats = n_seats, gal)

ltab(by_district,
     caption = paste0("Gallagher index within each electoral district, 2022: the ",
                      "district's own seats against its own registered voters. Each row ",
                      "is a separate index computed on that district's totals, so the ",
                      "values are comparable with one another but do not aggregate."),
     label = "gal-by-district",
     col.names = c("District", "Seats", "Gallagher"),
     digits = c(0, 0, 2))
```

## 5.3 Malapportionment by district and confession

```{r mal-grid, comment = ""}
tot_v    <- sum(dc$voters)
dev_cell <- dc |> mutate(quota = 128 * voters / tot_v, dev = seats - quota)

# Which cells actually return a member. Built in the same row and column order as the
# grids below, and used by both of them to mark the 59 cells that hold a seat apart from
# the 121 that have voters but none.
has_seat <- dc |>
  mutate(held = seats > 0) |> select(district, faith, held) |> arrange(district) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = district, values_from = held) |> arrange(faith)
seat_mask <- cbind(as.matrix(has_seat[, -1]), Total = FALSE)   # totals never bolded here
seat_mask <- rbind(seat_mask, rep(FALSE, ncol(seat_mask)))     # nor the summary row

mal_grid <- dev_cell |>
  select(district, faith, dev) |> arrange(district) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = district, values_from = dev) |>
  arrange(faith) |>
  mutate(Total = rowSums(pick(where(is.numeric))))
mal_grid <- bind_rows(mal_grid,
                      summarise(mal_grid, across(where(is.numeric), sum)) |>
                        mutate(faith = "All confessions")) |>
  relocate(faith)

# Three different misallocation counts live in this table, and they are not the same
# number: the interior gives the cell figure, the row totals the confessional one, the
# column totals the geographic one.
seats_wrong      <- sum(abs(dev_cell$dev)) / 2                       # 180 interior cells
seats_wrong_conf <- sum(abs(mal_grid$Total[-nrow(mal_grid)])) / 2    # 12 row totals
seats_wrong_geo  <- sum(abs(unlist(mal_grid[nrow(mal_grid), 2:16]))) / 2  # 15 col totals

# The corner is the sum of the row totals and of the column totals alike, and is always
# zero - every surplus is someone else's deficit. It carries no information and sits
# exactly where a reader looks for the headline, so it is checked and then left blank.
stopifnot(abs(mal_grid$Total[nrow(mal_grid)]) < 1e-9)
mal_grid$Total[nrow(mal_grid)] <- NA_real_

ltab(mal_grid,
     caption = "Malapportioned seats in status quo by confession and district, 2022.",
     note = paste0("Districts are abbreviated as in Table \\ref{tab:voters-per-seat}. ",
                   "Malapportioned seats computed by subtracting the seats allocated to a ",
                   "given confession in a district from the proportion of seats that would be ",
                   "allocated to that subgroup by share of population."),
     label = "mal-grid",
     col.names = c("Confession", DABBR[names(mal_grid)[2:16]], "Total"),
     digits = 2, fit = TRUE, bold_cells = seat_mask,
     bold_row = nrow(mal_grid), bold_col = ncol(mal_grid))

# Everything is recoverable from this grid. A seat is 100/128 of a percentage point, so
# each seat count is its index times 1.28.
stopifnot(
  abs(seats_wrong      - score(dc, c("district", "faith")) * 1.28) < 1e-9,
  abs(seats_wrong_conf - score(dc, "faith")    * 1.28)             < 1e-9,
  abs(seats_wrong_geo  - score(dc, "district") * 1.28)             < 1e-9,
  abs(sqrt(sum(dev_cell$dev^2) / 2) / 1.28 -
        score_g(dc, c("district", "faith")))                       < 1e-9)

cat(sprintf("\nseats in the wrong cell      %5.1f\nwrong confession nationally  %5.1f\nwrong district nationally    %5.1f\n",
            seats_wrong, seats_wrong_conf, seats_wrong_geo))
```

## 5.4 The same grid, as shares of the Gallagher index

```{r gal-grid, comment = ""}
gal_cell <- dc |>
  mutate(dev = 100 * seats / 128 - 100 * voters / tot_v) |>
  mutate(share = 100 * dev^2 / sum(dev^2))

gal_grid <- gal_cell |>
  select(district, faith, share) |> arrange(district) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = district, values_from = share) |>
  arrange(faith) |>
  mutate(Total = rowSums(pick(where(is.numeric))))
gal_grid <- bind_rows(gal_grid,
                      summarise(gal_grid, across(where(is.numeric), sum)) |>
                        mutate(faith = "All confessions")) |>
  relocate(faith)

ltab(gal_grid,
     caption = paste0("Share of the district-by-confession Gallagher score, in percent, ",
                      "by confession and district, 2022. Districts are abbreviated as in ",
                      "Table \\ref{tab:voters-per-seat}."),
     note = paste0("Each entry is the cell's contribution to the squared index, so the ",
                   "entries sum to 100."),
     label = "gal-grid",
     col.names = c("Confession", DABBR[names(gal_grid)[2:16]], "Total"),
     digits = 1, fit = TRUE, bold_cells = seat_mask,
     bold_row = nrow(gal_grid), bold_col = ncol(gal_grid))

# The shares decompose the SQUARE of the index, so a margin returns to Gallagher units by
# taking the root: sqrt(share/100) * G is that unit's slice, and the slices combine in
# quadrature to G itself.
G_cell <- score_g(dc, c("district", "faith"))
slices <- sqrt(gal_cell |> summarise(s = sum(dev^2) / 2, .by = district) |> pull(s))
stopifnot(abs(sum(gal_cell$share) - 100) < 1e-9,
          abs(sqrt(sum(slices^2)) - G_cell) < 1e-9,
          abs(gal_grid$Total[nrow(gal_grid)] - 100) < 1e-9)
```

## 5.5 The best allocation under the 64-64 rule

```{r optima, comment = ""}
BL <- c(Sunni = "Muslim", Shia = "Muslim", Druze = "Muslim", Alawite = "Muslim",
        Maronite = "Christian", `Greek Catholic` = "Christian",
        `Greek Orthodox` = "Christian", Protestant = "Christian",
        `Armenian Catholic` = "Christian", `Armenian Orthodox` = "Christian",
        `Christian Minorities` = "Christian", Other = "Other")
cv <- tibble(key = key180, district = cells$district, vfaith = cells$faith,
             s0 = S0, v = V0) |>
  filter(v > 0) |> mutate(bloc = unname(BL[vfaith]), quota = 128 * v / sum(v))
ix_cv <- function(sv) { S <- rep(0, length(key180)); S[match(cv$key, key180)] <- sv; indices(S) }

di <- match(cv$district, unname(DISTRICT)); fi <- match(cv$vfaith, faiths12)
agg_l <- function(x, m, k) as.vector(tapply(x, factor(m, levels = seq_len(k)), sum, default = 0))
Qd <- agg_l(cv$quota, di, 15); Qf <- agg_l(cv$quota, fi, 12)

# Moving a seat i -> j changes sum(s-q)^2 at a level by 2[(s_j-q_j)-(s_i-q_i)]+2, counted
# only where i and j differ at that level. All three are analytic, so every legal move can
# be scored at once.
optimise_idx <- function(which_idx, max_k = 60) {
  s <- cv$s0
  for (step in seq_len(max_k)) {
    d  <- s - cv$quota
    Sd <- agg_l(s, di, 15) - Qd; Sf <- agg_l(s, fi, 12) - Qf
    prim <- switch(which_idx,
      cell = outer(-d, d, "+"),
      geo  = { m <- outer(-Sd[di], Sd[di], "+"); m[outer(di, di, "==")] <- NA; m },
      conf = { m <- outer(-Sf[fi], Sf[fi], "+"); m[outer(fi, fi, "==")] <- NA; m })
    prim <- 2 * prim + 2
    tie  <- 2 * outer(-d, d, "+") + 2
    legal <- outer(s >= 1, rep(TRUE, length(s))) & outer(cv$bloc, cv$bloc, "==")
    diag(legal) <- FALSE
    prim[!legal] <- NA; tie[!legal] <- NA
    prim[is.na(prim)] <- 0                       # neutral at this level
    cand <- which(prim < -1e-9 | (abs(prim) < 1e-9 & tie < -1e-9))
    if (!length(cand)) break
    best <- cand[order(prim[cand], tie[cand])[1]]
    i <- ((best - 1) %% nrow(prim)) + 1; j <- ((best - 1) %/% nrow(prim)) + 1
    s[i] <- s[i] - 1L; s[j] <- s[j] + 1L
  }
  s
}

opt <- map(set_names(c("geo", "conf", "cell")), optimise_idx)
z0  <- ix_cv(cv$s0)

# The unconstrained optimum, for reference: no bloc constraint at all, seats handed out one
# at a time to whichever cell gains most. Both |s - q| and (s - q)^2 are convex in s, so a
# one-at-a-time allocation from zero is exactly optimal - and here the two objectives
# return the same table, so one calculation serves for both indices.
greedy_free <- function(q, total, obj = c("L2", "L1")) {
  obj <- match.arg(obj); s <- rep(0L, length(q))
  for (k in seq_len(total)) {
    gain <- if (obj == "L2") (s + 1 - q)^2 - (s - q)^2 else abs(s + 1 - q) - abs(s - q)
    i <- which.min(gain); s[i] <- s[i] + 1L
  }
  s
}
free_cell <- greedy_free(cv$quota, 128L, "L2")
stopifnot(identical(free_cell, greedy_free(cv$quota, 128L, "L1")))   # the two agree here

# --- one national district ----------------------------------------------------
# Abolishing the districts collapses the 180 cells onto the 12 confessions, so the seat
# table is a national confessional quota and nothing else. Two consequences, both by
# construction rather than by merit: the single district holds 100 per cent of the seats
# and 100 per cent of the voters, so geographic malapportionment is exactly zero; and the
# cell index becomes the confessional index, because the cells are now the confessions.
hamilton <- function(v, total) {
  q <- total * v / sum(v); w <- floor(q); left <- total - sum(w)
  if (left > 0) { i <- order(q - w, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(left)]; w[i] <- w[i] + 1L }
  as.integer(w)
}
natl <- dc |> summarise(v = sum(voters), s0 = sum(seats), .by = faith) |>
  mutate(bloc = unname(BL[faith]), q = 128 * v / sum(v)) |> arrange(faith)

# Parity kept: each bloc's 64 seats shared out in proportion to that bloc's own voters,
# which is what a national district under the 64-64 rule would mean in practice.
natl$parity <- 0L
for (b in c("Christian", "Muslim")) {
  k <- natl$bloc == b; natl$parity[k] <- hamilton(natl$v[k], 64L)
}
natl$free <- hamilton(natl$v, 128L)
stopifnot(sum(natl$parity) == 128, sum(natl$free) == 128,
          sum(natl$parity[natl$bloc == "Christian"]) == 64)

natl_row <- function(col, lab)
  tibble(minimised = lab,
         moves = sum(abs(natl[[col]] - natl$s0)) / 2, districts = NA_integer_,
         gal_geo = 0, gal_conf = gallagher(natl[[col]], natl$v),
         gal_cell = gallagher(natl[[col]], natl$v),
         mal_cell = mal(natl[[col]], natl$v),
         mal_seats = mal(natl[[col]], natl$v) * 1.28)
optab <- imap_dfr(opt, function(s, nm) {
  z <- ix_cv(s)
  tibble(minimised = c(geo = "Geographic", conf = "Confessional", cell = "Cell")[[nm]],
         moves = sum(abs(s - cv$s0)) / 2,
         districts = n_distinct(cv$district[s != cv$s0]),
         gal_geo = z[["gal_geo"]], gal_conf = z[["gal_conf"]], gal_cell = z[["gal_cell"]],
         mal_cell = z[["mal_cell"]], mal_seats = z[["mal_cell"]] * 1.28)
})

# The table shows three seat tables: today's, the best attainable under the 64-64 rule, and
# one national district. The other optima computed above - geographic, confessional, and
# the two parity-dropped variants - are reported in the prose instead, since they are
# reference points rather than proposals.
# One helper so the status-quo row and the parity-dropped row are built the same way: neither
# comes out of `opt`, which holds only the parity-respecting optima.
opt_row <- function(sv, label) {
  z <- ix_cv(sv)
  tibble(table = label,
         moves = sum(abs(sv - cv$s0)) / 2,
         districts = n_distinct(cv$district[sv != cv$s0]),
         gal_geo = z[["gal_geo"]], gal_conf = z[["gal_conf"]], gal_cell = z[["gal_cell"]],
         mal_cell = z[["mal_cell"]], mal_seats = z[["mal_cell"]] * 1.28)
}

# The parity-dropped row sits SECOND, immediately under the status quo: read down the first three
# rows and the 64-64 rule's cost is the gap between rows 2 and 3, on a common baseline. It is a
# BOUND on what is attainable, not a proposal.
optab <- bind_rows(
  opt_row(cv$s0, "Status Quo"),
  opt_row(free_cell, "Proportional Ideal (without Taif Agreement)"),
  optab |> filter(minimised == "Cell") |>
    mutate(minimised = "Best Alternative (with Taif Agreement)") |> rename(table = minimised),
  # Two single-district rows. The first dissolves the districts and keeps today's twelve
  # confessional totals, so it moves no seats; the second also recomputes those totals within
  # each bloc (section 5.7 takes the two apart).
  natl_row("s0", "Single National District (Status Quo Allocation)") |> rename(table = minimised),
  natl_row("parity", "Single National District (Reallocation)") |> rename(table = minimised))

stopifnot(nrow(optab) == 5L,
          optab$moves[1] == 0, optab$districts[1] == 0,
          # the status-quo row must reproduce the figures section 4 reports
          abs(optab$gal_cell[1] - z0[["gal_cell"]]) < 1e-9,
          # the parity-dropped row drops parity: 41 Christian to 87 Muslim
          sum(free_cell[cv$bloc == "Christian"]) == 41L,
          sum(free_cell[cv$bloc == "Muslim"]) == 87L,
          identical(optab$table[2], "Proportional Ideal (without Taif Agreement)"),   # second line
          # dissolving the districts alone moves no seats and leaves the confessional index as is
          optab$moves[4] == 0, optab$gal_geo[4] == 0,
          abs(optab$gal_conf[4] - z0[["gal_conf"]]) < 1e-9,
          # and it is strictly better than the parity-respecting optimum on the cell index
          optab$gal_cell[2] < optab$gal_cell[3])

# The table is emitted at the end of section 6, once the diaspora scenarios it also carries
# have been built. Nothing is printed here.
```

## 5.6 What the best alternative allocation changes

```{r opt-grid, comment = ""}
# Seat change per cell, and the Gallagher slice of any group of cells, before and after.
optcells <- cv |> mutate(new = opt$cell, d = new - s0,
                         dev0 = 100 * s0  / 128 - 100 * v / sum(cv$v),
                         dev1 = 100 * new / 128 - 100 * v / sum(cv$v))
slice_delta <- function(g) sqrt(sum(g$dev1^2) / 2) - sqrt(sum(g$dev0^2) / 2)
d_gal <- function(by) optcells |> group_by(across(all_of(by))) |>
  group_modify(\(g, k) tibble(dgal = slice_delta(g))) |> ungroup() |> arrange(.data[[by]])

# The body holds whole seats and two of the margins hold Gallagher changes; `digits`
# applies down a whole column, so the table is assembled as text, each part formatted its
# own way.
as_seats <- function(x) if_else(is.na(x), "", formatC(x, format = "d"))
as_gal   <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3)

by_faith_seats <- optcells |> summarise(net = sum(d), .by = vfaith) |> arrange(vfaith)
by_dist_seats  <- optcells |> summarise(net = sum(d), .by = district) |> arrange(district)
by_faith_gal   <- d_gal("vfaith")
by_dist_gal    <- d_gal("district")
stopifnot(sum(by_faith_seats$net) == 0, sum(by_dist_seats$net) == 0)   # it is a swap

opt_grid <- optcells |>
  mutate(cell = if_else(s0 == 0 & new == 0, NA_real_, as.numeric(d))) |>
  select(district, vfaith, cell) |> arrange(district) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = district, values_from = cell) |> arrange(vfaith) |>
  mutate(across(-vfaith, as_seats),
         Seats = as_seats(by_faith_seats$net), Gallagher = as_gal(by_faith_gal$dgal))

# Two summary rows: net seats by district, then that district's change in Gallagher. Only
# the second has a meaningful corner - net seats necessarily sum to zero, so that cell is
# left blank rather than printed as a nought.
mk_row <- function(label, vals, seats = "", gal = "")
  as_tibble(c(list(vfaith = label), as.list(vals),
              list(Seats = seats, Gallagher = gal)))
opt_grid <- bind_rows(
  opt_grid,
  mk_row("Net change", setNames(as_seats(by_dist_seats$net), by_dist_seats$district)),
  mk_row("Change in Gallagher", setNames(as_gal(by_dist_gal$dgal), by_dist_gal$district),
         gal = as_gal(slice_delta(optcells))))

# Bold the cells that change, and both margin columns. The two summary rows are bolded by
# bold_row, so they are FALSE here and \textbf never nests.
chg_mask <- optcells |>
  mutate(chg = d != 0) |> select(district, vfaith, chg) |> arrange(district) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = district, values_from = chg) |> arrange(vfaith)
chg_mask <- cbind(as.matrix(chg_mask[, -1]), Seats = TRUE, Gallagher = TRUE)
chg_mask[is.na(chg_mask)] <- FALSE      # the one pair with no registrants anywhere
chg_mask <- rbind(chg_mask, rep(FALSE, ncol(chg_mask)), rep(FALSE, ncol(chg_mask)))

ltab(opt_grid,
     caption = paste0("Seats gained and lost from Status Quo to Best Alternative under ",
                      "Taif Agreement."),
     note = "Districts are abbreviated as in Table \\ref{tab:voters-per-seat}.",
     label = "opt-grid",
     col.names = c("Confession", DABBR[names(opt_grid)[2:16]], "Net Change", "Gallagher"),
     align = paste0("l", strrep("r", 17)), fit = TRUE,
     bold_cells = chg_mask, bold_row = c(nrow(opt_grid) - 1L, nrow(opt_grid)))

stopifnot(sum(abs(optcells$d)) / 2 == 27,
          abs(slice_delta(optcells) -
                (ix_cv(opt$cell)[["gal_cell"]] - z0[["gal_cell"]])) < 1e-9)
```

```{r opt-detail, comment = ""}

netchange_tab <- bind_rows(

    arrange(desc(net)) |> transmute(grouping = "Confession", unit = vfaith, net),
  ch |> summarise(net = sum(d), .by = district) |> filter(net != 0) |>

# The grouping column becomes pack_rows subheadings, which reads better in print and
# needs only \multicolumn.
ltab(netchange_tab |> select(-grouping),
```
