## 5.7 What one national district changes

```{r natl-decomp, comment = ""}
# One national district with TWO seat tables: today's confessional totals kept as they are
# (`natl$s0`), and the within-bloc proportional recomputation (`natl$parity`) that section 5.5
# reports. With one district the twelve confessions ARE the cells, so a single formula serves.
nd_ix <- function(sv) {
  dev <- 100 * sv / sum(sv) - 100 * natl$v / sum(natl$v)
  c(mal = sum(abs(dev)) / 2, gal = sqrt(sum(dev^2) / 2))
}
nd_sq <- nd_ix(natl$s0); nd_pa <- nd_ix(natl$parity)

# Geographic malapportionment is exactly zero for BOTH single-district rows, by construction and
# not by merit: one unit holds 100 per cent of the seats and 100 per cent of the voters.
natl_decomp <- tibble(
  scenario  = c("Status quo, fifteen districts", "One district, present seat table",
                "One district, seats recomputed in bloc"),
  districts = c(15L, 1L, 1L),
  moves     = c(0L, 0L, as.integer(sum(abs(natl$parity - natl$s0)) / 2)),
  mal_geo   = c(score(dc, "district"), 0, 0),
  gal_geo   = c(score_g(dc, "district"), 0, 0),
  mal_conf  = c(score(dc, "faith"),   nd_sq[["mal"]], nd_pa[["mal"]]),
  gal_conf  = c(score_g(dc, "faith"), nd_sq[["gal"]], nd_pa[["gal"]]))

# The whole point of the first two rows: abolishing the districts moves the CONFESSIONAL index
# not at all, because confessional totals are a property of the seat table and not of how the
# districts are drawn. Asserted rather than asserted in prose only.
stopifnot(
  all.equal(nd_sq[["mal"]], base_ix[["mal_conf"]]),
  all.equal(nd_sq[["gal"]], base_ix[["gal_conf"]]),
  natl_decomp$moves[2] == 0L, natl_decomp$moves[3] == 7L,
  # and the reallocation half moves the GEOGRAPHIC index not at all - it is already zero
  natl_decomp$gal_geo[2] == natl_decomp$gal_geo[3],
  # parity is respected in both single-district tables
  sum(natl$s0[natl$bloc == "Christian"]) == 64L,
  sum(natl$parity[natl$bloc == "Christian"]) == 64L)

ltab(natl_decomp,
     caption = paste0("One national district, taken apart. The second row abolishes the ",
       "districts and changes nothing else - the twelve confessional totals stay exactly as ",
       "they are today - and the third then recomputes those totals in proportion to each ",
       "bloc's own voters, keeping 64--64. \\emph{Moves} counts the seats that change hands ",
       "relative to the present table. Geographic malapportionment is zero in both ",
       "single-district rows \\emph{by construction}, one unit holding all the seats and all ",
       "the voters, and with one district the twelve confessions are the cells, so the cell ",
       "index equals the confessional one and is not shown separately. Confessional figures ",
       "are comparable down the column: there are twelve confessions in every row."),
     label = "natl-decomp",
     col.names = c("Scenario", "Districts", "Seat moves", "SLH: geographic",
                   "Gallagher: geographic", "SLH: confessional",
                   "Gallagher: confessional"),
     align = "lrrrrrr", digits = c(0, 0, 0, 2, 3, 2, 3))
```

```{r natl-grid, comment = ""}
# Same shape as the grid in 5.6, with the fifteen district columns collapsed into the one
# that remains.
#
# The Gallagher column is measured at the CONFESSIONAL level on both sides. It has to be:
# a national district has twelve cells where the current table has 180, and Gallagher is
# not monotone under refinement (section 1), so comparing 5.358 over 180 cells with 9.494
# over twelve would mostly measure the change of units. At the confessional level the two
# tables are directly comparable, and the slices still combine in quadrature - to 10.629
# before and 9.494 after.
natl_cells <- natl |>
  mutate(d = parity - s0,
         dev0 = 100 * s0     / 128 - 100 * v / tot_v,
         dev1 = 100 * parity / 128 - 100 * v / tot_v,
         s_before = sqrt(dev0^2 / 2), s_after = sqrt(dev1^2 / 2),
         dgal = s_after - s_before) |>
  arrange(faith)

as_seats <- function(x) if_else(is.na(x), "", formatC(x, format = "d"))
as_gal   <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3)
gal_tot  <- sqrt(sum(natl_cells$s_after^2)) - sqrt(sum(natl_cells$s_before^2))

natl_grid <- natl_cells |>
  transmute(faith,
            nat = as_seats(if_else(s0 == 0 & parity == 0, NA_integer_, as.integer(d))),
            net = as_seats(if_else(s0 == 0 & parity == 0, NA_integer_, as.integer(d))),
            Gallagher = as_gal(dgal))

# Foot rows. The district margin reports how many seats change hands, not the net: the one
# district holds all 128 seats before and after, so its net is necessarily zero and would
# say nothing. Half the sum of the absolute changes is the count that actually moves,
# matching how seats moved is counted everywhere else in this section.
natl_grid <- bind_rows(
  natl_grid,
  tibble(faith = "Seats changed", nat = as_seats(sum(abs(natl_cells$d)) / 2),
         net = "", Gallagher = ""),
  tibble(faith = "Change in Gallagher", nat = as_gal(gal_tot),
         net = "", Gallagher = as_gal(gal_tot)))

natl_mask <- rbind(cbind(natl_cells$d != 0, TRUE, TRUE), rep(FALSE, 3), rep(FALSE, 3))

ltab(natl_grid,
     caption = paste0("Seats gained and lost with a Single National District ",
                      "(With Reallocation)"),
     label = "natl-grid",
     col.names = c("Confession", "National District", "Net Change",
                   "Gallagher (Confessional)"),
     align = "lrrr", bold_cells = natl_mask,
     bold_row = c(nrow(natl_grid) - 1L, nrow(natl_grid)))

stopifnot(sum(natl$parity) == 128, sum(natl_cells$d) == 0,   # a swap: the net is zero
          sum(abs(natl_cells$d)) / 2 == 7,                   # but seven seats move
          abs(sqrt(sum(natl_cells$s_before^2)) - score_g(dc, "faith"))           < 1e-9,
          abs(sqrt(sum(natl_cells$s_after^2))  - gallagher(natl$parity, natl$v)) < 1e-9)
```

# 6. A separate diaspora district

## 6.1 Three scenarios

```{r dia-alloc, comment = ""}
# Diaspora registrants are `registered_total - registered_resident`, already carried in `dc`
# from section 2. The country x district x sect file is a strict refinement of the same counts;
# it is read here to CHECK that and to report where the electorate sits, which nothing else in
# this document shows.
dia_ctry <- read.csv(
  "data/population - registered voters/diaspora_voters_by_country_district_sect.csv",
  fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM") |>
  mutate(district = unname(DISTRICT[major_district]), faith = sect_en)

# Checked at BOTH grains. The country file resolves to minor district x sect, the grain
# `voters_by_district_sect_long.csv` is published at, so the 299-cell agreement there is the
# strong check; `dc` is aggregated to the fifteen major districts and can only be checked on
# its own 180-cell grid. Neither file stores a row for a cell with nobody in it, so the missing
# side is filled with 0 rather than counted as a disagreement.
vlong <- read.csv("data/population - registered voters/voters_by_district_sect_long.csv",
                  fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
zjoin <- function(a, b, by) full_join(a, b, by = by) |>
  mutate(across(c(a, b), \(x) replace_na(x, 0)))
chk_minor <- zjoin(summarise(dia_ctry, a = sum(registered_diaspora),
                             .by = c(minor_district_en, sect_en)),
                   summarise(vlong, b = sum(registered_total - registered_resident),
                             .by = c(minor_district_en, sect_en)),
                   c("minor_district_en", "sect_en"))
chk_major <- zjoin(summarise(dia_ctry, a = sum(registered_diaspora), .by = c(district, faith)),
                   summarise(dc, b = sum(voters - residents), .by = c(district, faith)),
                   c("district", "faith"))
stopifnot(nrow(vlong) == 299, nrow(chk_minor) == 299, all(chk_minor$a == chk_minor$b),
          nrow(chk_major) == 180, all(chk_major$a == chk_major$b))

DIA   <- "diaspora"
dia_f <- dc |>
  summarise(v = sum(voters - residents), res = sum(residents), .by = faith) |>
  mutate(bloc = unname(BL[faith])) |>
  arrange(faith)
stopifnot(sum(dia_f$v) == sum(dia_ctry$registered_diaspora), sum(dia_f$v) == 225624)

# `Other` holds no seat anywhere in the current table and is not given one here, so the seat
# allocation runs over the eleven confessions that do. Its registrants stay in every voter
# denominator, exactly as section 2 keeps them in `dc`.
seatable <- dia_f$bloc != "Other"

# S: Article 112 NAMES the six sects - one seat each to Maronite, Greek Orthodox, Greek
# Catholic, Sunni, Shia and Druze - so there is no allocation rule to apply. An earlier version
# of this chunk shared three seats per bloc by largest remainder on that bloc's own registrants,
# which gave Maronites two and Greek Catholics none; that is not what the statute says.
STAT6 <- c("Maronite", "Greek Orthodox", "Greek Catholic", "Sunni", "Shia", "Druze")
stopifnot(all(STAT6 %in% dia_f$faith))
dia_f$s_S <- as.integer(dia_f$faith %in% STAT6)

# P: seven seats by largest remainder across all eleven seat-holding confessions at once, so
# the bloc split falls out rather than being imposed.
dia_f$s_P <- 0L
dia_f$s_P[seatable] <- hamilton(dia_f$v[seatable], 7L)

dia_bloc <- function(col) c(
  Christian = sum(dia_f[[col]][dia_f$bloc == "Christian"]),
  Muslim    = sum(dia_f[[col]][dia_f$bloc == "Muslim"]))
stopifnot(sum(dia_f$s_S) == 6L, sum(dia_f$s_P) == 7L,
          all(dia_bloc("s_S") == c(3L, 3L)),      # named by statute, sect by sect
          all(dia_bloc("s_P") == c(4L, 3L)),      # an output of the diaspora roll
          # the statute's six sects are exactly the six largest confessions abroad
          setequal(STAT6, (dia_f |> filter(bloc != "Other") |> slice_max(v, n = 6))$faith),
          # and P differs from S by exactly one seat, a second Maronite one
          sum(abs(dia_f$s_P - dia_f$s_S)) == 1L,
          dia_f$s_P[dia_f$faith == "Maronite"] - dia_f$s_S[dia_f$faith == "Maronite"] == 1L)

alloc_tab <- dia_f |>
  filter(v > 0) |>
  transmute(faith, bloc,
            registrants = v,
            pct_dia = 100 * v / sum(dia_f$v),
            pct_res = 100 * res / sum(dia_f$res),
            # `Other` is outside the seat allocation, so it has no quota rather than a
            # quota of zero; the seat-holding confessions' quotas sum to exactly 6 and 7.
            # Under S the quota is what the sect WOULD be owed - the statute ignores it and
            # awards one seat each to six named sects, so the gap column is the distortion.
            q_S = if_else(bloc == "Other", NA_real_, 6 * v / sum(dia_f$v[seatable])), s_S,
            gap_S = if_else(bloc == "Other", NA_real_, s_S - 6 * v / sum(dia_f$v[seatable])),
            q_P = if_else(bloc == "Other", NA_real_, 7 * v / sum(dia_f$v[seatable])), s_P) |>
  arrange(desc(registrants))

alloc_tab <- bind_rows(alloc_tab, tibble(
  faith = "Total", bloc = "", registrants = sum(dia_f$v), pct_dia = 100, pct_res = 100,
  q_S = 6, s_S = sum(dia_f$s_S), gap_S = 0, q_P = 7, s_P = sum(dia_f$s_P)))
stopifnot(all.equal(sum(alloc_tab$q_S, na.rm = TRUE), 12),   # body sums to 6, plus the foot
          all.equal(sum(alloc_tab$q_P, na.rm = TRUE), 14))

ltab(alloc_tab,
     caption = paste0("The diaspora district's seats by confession, 2022 register. ",
       "\\emph{Share of roll} columns compare each confession's weight among the 225,624 ",
       "registrants abroad with its weight among the 3,741,883 resident registrants: the ",
       "diaspora roll is 52.8 per cent Christian against 33.2 per cent at home, and ",
       "Maronites are 32.1 per cent of it. \\emph{Quota} is the confession's exact claim on ",
       "the six or seven seats, over the eleven confessions that hold a seat anywhere in the ",
       "current table (\\emph{Other} is not given one, and keeps its registrants in the ",
       "denominator). Scenario S is Article 112 as written: one seat each to six \\emph{named} ",
       "sects, so the \\emph{Gap} column is the distortion that fixed award imposes, not a ",
       "rounding residue. Scenario P allocates all seven by largest remainder, so its 4--3 ",
       "bloc split is an output. The statute's six sects are exactly the six largest ",
       "confessions abroad, and P differs from S by a single seat -- a second Maronite one."),
     label = "dia-alloc",
     col.names = c("Confession", "Bloc", "Registrants abroad", "% of diaspora roll",
                   "% of resident roll", "Quota (6)", "S", "Gap", "Quota (7)", "P"),
     align = "llrrrrrrrr", digits = c(0, 0, 0, 2, 2, 2, 0, 2, 2, 0), fit = TRUE,
     bold_row = nrow(alloc_tab))
```

## 6.2 Which domestic seats pay for the diaspora district

```{r dia-carve, comment = ""}
# Removing a seat from cell i changes sum(s - q)^2 by -2(s_i - q_i) + 1, so the seat to take is
# always the one in the cell furthest above its quota. The objective is separable and convex in
# s, so removing them one at a time is exactly optimal - the argument section 5.5 makes for the
# greedy reallocation there, run in reverse. The blocs are independent: the quota is fixed, so
# drawing one bloc down cannot change which cell is chosen in the other.
drop_from_bloc <- function(s, q, bloc, n_by_bloc) {
  for (b in names(n_by_bloc)) for (k in seq_len(n_by_bloc[[b]])) {
    i <- which(bloc == b & s >= 1L)
    stopifnot(length(i) > 0L)
    i <- i[which.max((s - q)[i])]
    s[i] <- s[i] - 1L
  }
  s
}

dom <- dc |>
  select(district, dist_name, faith, seats, voters, residents) |>
  mutate(bloc = unname(BL[faith])) |>
  arrange(district, faith)
M_dom_P  <- 128L - sum(dia_f$s_P)                                        # 121
dom$q_P  <- M_dom_P * dom$residents / sum(dom$residents)
dom$s_P  <- drop_from_bloc(as.integer(dom$seats), dom$q_P, dom$bloc,
                           as.list(dia_bloc("s_P")))

# --- the fold-in phase: the statutory SIX inside 128, so the domestic table drops to 122 ----
# The article returns the six seats "from the same confessions" they were awarded to, so the
# CONFESSION of each withdrawal is fixed by statute - one seat back from each of the six named
# sects - and only the DISTRICT is free. That choice is made by minimising Gallagher within the
# confession, which is the same rule used for P7 below.
#
# Minimising sum((s - q)^2) IS minimising Gallagher: with q = T * v / sum(v) a cell's deviation
# is dev = (100/T)(s - q), so at a fixed chamber size the two objectives differ only by a
# positive constant and the same withdrawal is optimal for both.
#
# Note parity comes free here: the six named sects are three Christian and three Muslim, so
# taking one seat from each holds the national 64-64 without a bloc constraint being imposed.
M_dom_F <- 128L - sum(dia_f$s_S)                                         # 122
dom$q_F <- M_dom_F * dom$residents / sum(dom$residents)

s_F <- as.integer(dom$seats)
for (f in STAT6) {
  i <- which(dom$faith == f & s_F >= 1L)
  j <- i[which.max((s_F - dom$q_F)[i])]
  s_F[j] <- s_F[j] - 1L
}
dom$s_F <- s_F

stopifnot(sum(dom$s_P) == M_dom_P, all(dom$s_P >= 0L),
          sum(dom$seats - dom$s_P) == 7L,
          sum(dom$s_F) == M_dom_F, all(dom$s_F >= 0L),
          sum(dom$seats - dom$s_F) == 6L,
          # parity holds at 64-64 without being imposed - the six named sects are 3C/3M
          sum(dom$s_F[dom$bloc == "Christian"]) + dia_bloc("s_S")[["Christian"]] == 64L,
          sum(dom$s_F[dom$bloc == "Muslim"])    + dia_bloc("s_S")[["Muslim"]]    == 64L,
          # S128 is confessionally NEUTRAL BY CONSTRUCTION: it hands each named sect one diaspora
          # seat and takes one domestic seat back from that same sect, so no confession's
          # national total moves at all. Checked, not assumed.
          {
            nb <- summarise(dc, s = sum(seats), .by = faith) |> arrange(faith)
            ng <- bind_rows(transmute(dom, faith, s = s_F),
                            transmute(dia_f, faith, s = s_S)) |>
                  summarise(s = sum(s), .by = faith) |> arrange(faith)
            identical(nb$faith, ng$faith) && all(nb$s == ng$s)
          },
          # national parity: 64-64 under P, 67-67 under S
          sum(dom$s_P[dom$bloc == "Christian"]) + dia_bloc("s_P")[["Christian"]] == 64L,
          sum(dom$s_P[dom$bloc == "Muslim"])    + dia_bloc("s_P")[["Muslim"]]    == 64L,
          sum(dom$seats[dom$bloc == "Christian"]) + dia_bloc("s_S")[["Christian"]] == 67L,
          sum(dom$seats[dom$bloc == "Muslim"])    + dia_bloc("s_S")[["Muslim"]]    == 67L)

# One row per cell that any of the three fundings touches, so the three can be compared at a
# glance. A blank means that scenario leaves the cell alone.
carve <- dom |>
  filter(s_P != seats | s_F != seats) |>
  transmute(dist_name, faith, bloc, seats, residents,
            d_F = as.integer(s_F - seats), d_P = as.integer(s_P - seats),
            surplus = seats - q_P) |>
  arrange(bloc, desc(surplus))
blank0 <- function(x) if_else(x == 0L, "", formatC(x, format = "d"))
carve_out <- carve |> mutate(across(c(d_F, d_P), blank0))
stopifnot(sum(carve$d_P) == -7L, sum(carve$d_F) == -6L)

ltab(carve_out |> select(-bloc),
     caption = paste0("The domestic seats each funding takes, one row per cell any of them ",
       "touches, Christian cells first. \\emph{Surplus} is how far the cell sits above its ",
       "claim on 121 seats measured against resident registrants only. Blank means the scenario ",
       "leaves the cell alone. The two differ in kind, not just in size: S128 must take one seat ",
       "back from each of the six sects Article 112 names, so it reaches Greek Orthodox, Greek ",
       "Catholic and Sunni cells; P7 is free to follow the index and so concentrates on the most ",
       "diaspora-heavy Maronite cells, taking two from Mount Lebanon I. The Druze cell in Beirut ",
       "II and the Alawite cell in North I would lose their district's only seat of that ",
       "confession - a larger change than the arithmetic shows, see the caution below."),
     label = "dia-carve",
     col.names = c("District", "Confession", "Seats now", "Resident registrants",
                   "S128", "P7", "Surplus"),
     align = "llrrrrr", digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 2), fit = TRUE)
```

## 6.3 What the reform does to the indices

```{r dia-index, comment = ""}
# `indices()` in section 3 is pinned to the fifteen-district, 180-cell status quo. A diaspora
# district adds a sixteenth unit, so the same arithmetic is written here over an arbitrary
# unit x faith table - and checked against `indices()` on the status quo before it is used on
# anything else.
ix3 <- function(d) {
  T <- sum(d$seats); V <- sum(d$v)
  lev <- function(by) {
    g   <- summarise(d, s = sum(seats), v = sum(v), .by = all_of(by))
    dev <- 100 * g$s / T - 100 * g$v / V
    c(mal = sum(abs(dev)) / 2, gal = sqrt(sum(dev^2) / 2))
  }
  g <- lev("district"); f <- lev("faith"); c2 <- lev(c("district", "faith"))
  c(mal_geo = g[["mal"]], mal_conf = f[["mal"]], mal_cell = c2[["mal"]],
    gal_cell = c2[["gal"]], gal_geo = g[["gal"]], gal_conf = f[["gal"]])
}
stopifnot(all.equal(ix3(mutate(dc, v = voters)), base_ix, tolerance = 1e-9))

# A 16 x 12 unit x faith table per scenario. The domestic side is scored on residents; the
# diaspora district holds the registrants those districts gave up, so every scenario is scored
# on the same 3,967,507 people, partitioned differently.
scen_tab <- function(dom_seats, dia_col) bind_rows(
  transmute(dom, district, dist_name, faith, seats = dom_seats, v = residents),
  transmute(dia_f, district = DIA, dist_name = "Diaspora", faith,
            seats = .data[[dia_col]], v = v))

# THE BASELINE IS THE STATUS QUO, and it lives on the same sixteen-unit grid as every scenario.
# That is not a trick: under the suspension the electorate abroad votes in its district of civil
# registration, so those voters ARE the domestic rows' registrants and the diaspora unit holds
# nobody and nothing. Writing it out that way - domestic cells on `voters` (the full roll,
# emigrants included), diaspora cells at zero voters and zero seats - gives a 192-cell table that
# is the status quo exactly. A cell with no voters and no seats contributes no deviation, which is
# why scoring it reproduces `base_ix` from section 3 to the last digit; that is asserted below
# rather than assumed. Every comparison in this section is therefore like-for-like: the same 192
# cells and the same 3,967,507 registrants on both sides, with only seats and their partition
# moving.
tab_sq <- bind_rows(
  transmute(dom,   district, dist_name, faith, seats = as.integer(seats), v = voters),
  transmute(dia_f, district = DIA, dist_name = "Diaspora", faith, seats = 0L, v = 0))

tab_S <- scen_tab(as.integer(dom$seats), "s_S")     # S134: added on, domestic untouched
tab_F <- scen_tab(dom$s_F,               "s_S")     # S128: folded in, same confessions
tab_P <- scen_tab(dom$s_P,               "s_P")     # P7: seven, proportional
stopifnot(sum(tab_sq$seats) == 128L, sum(tab_S$seats) == 134L, sum(tab_P$seats) == 128L,
          sum(tab_F$seats) == 128L,
          nrow(tab_sq) == 16 * 12, nrow(tab_S) == 16 * 12,
          all.equal(sum(tab_sq$v), sum(dc$voters)),
          all.equal(sum(tab_S$v), sum(dc$voters)), all.equal(sum(tab_P$v), sum(dc$voters)),
          # the 192-cell status quo IS the fifteen-district status quo, scored identically
          all.equal(ix3(tab_sq), base_ix, tolerance = 1e-9))

# The sixteen-unit voter vector the scenarios live on (diaspora holding its own registrants), for
# the granularity floors below. Identical across scenarios, so it is taken once.
v16 <- tab_P$v
stopifnot(identical(v16, tab_S$v), identical(v16, tab_F$v))

# A BENCHMARK row: section 5.5's best 128-seat reallocation inside the fifteen districts, with no
# diaspora district at all. It answers the obvious question about every row above - how much of the
# available improvement does a diaspora reform actually capture? - and it belongs on this grid for
# the same reason the status quo does: written with the diaspora unit empty it scores exactly as it
# does over 180 cells, which is asserted below.
#
# `opt$cell` is indexed over `cv` (the cells that have voters), so it is scattered back onto the
# 180-cell order. `dom` shares that order with `key180`, both being arrange(district, faith).
S_ba <- rep(0L, length(key180))
S_ba[match(cv$key, key180)] <- as.integer(opt$cell)
stopifnot(identical(paste(dom$district, dom$faith, sep = "|"), key180))
tab_ba <- bind_rows(
  transmute(dom, district, dist_name, faith, seats = S_ba, v = voters),
  transmute(dia_f, district = DIA, dist_name = "Diaspora", faith, seats = 0L, v = 0))
stopifnot(sum(tab_ba$seats) == 128L,
          # the 192-cell scorer must reproduce section 5.5's own figures exactly
          all.equal(ix3(tab_ba), ix_cv(opt$cell), tolerance = 1e-9))

# --- the granularity floor -----------------------------------------------------
# A 134-seat chamber is not scored on a different footing: both indices compare seat SHARES with
# voter SHARES and both sides are normalised to 100, so the changed member-to-voter ratio cancels
# out. What DOES change is the GRAIN - one seat is 1/134 of the chamber rather than 1/128 - and
# finer units track any target more closely. `floors` isolates exactly that, per measure: for a
# chamber of T it allocates T seats over the same sixteen-unit voter vector to minimise that
# measure, ignoring every confessional and parity constraint. SLH is an L1 index so its optimum
# is largest remainder; Gallagher is L2 so its optimum is the greedy L2 allocation. The gap
# between the T=128 and T=134 floors is the mechanical advantage the bigger chamber enjoys, and
# it is the yardstick for deciding which of S134's margins mean anything.
floors <- function(T) {
  v  <- v16
  di <- match(tab_P$district, unique(tab_P$district))     # 16 units
  fi <- match(tab_P$faith,    unique(tab_P$faith))        # 12 confessions
  ag <- function(x, m, k) as.vector(tapply(x, factor(m, levels = seq_len(k)), sum, default = 0))
  lev <- function(vv) {
    sh <- 100 * vv / sum(vv)
    c(mal = sum(abs(100 * hamilton(vv, T) / T - sh)) / 2,
      gal = sqrt(sum((100 * greedy_free(T * vv / sum(vv), T, "L2") / T - sh)^2) / 2))
  }
  g <- lev(ag(v, di, 16)); f <- lev(ag(v, fi, 12)); c2 <- lev(v)
  c(mal_geo = g[["mal"]], mal_conf = f[["mal"]], mal_cell = c2[["mal"]],
    gal_geo = g[["gal"]], gal_conf = f[["gal"]], gal_cell = c2[["gal"]])
}
IXM     <- c("mal_geo", "mal_conf", "mal_cell", "gal_geo", "gal_conf", "gal_cell")
gran    <- floors(128L) - floors(134L)
stopifnot(all(gran > 0))              # the larger chamber has the lower floor on every measure

dia_scores <- bind_rows(
  tibble(scenario = "Status Quo (No Diaspora District)", seats = 128L, dia = 0L,
         as_tibble_row(ix3(tab_sq))),
  tibble(scenario = "Article 112 Diaspora District (+6)", seats = 134L, dia = 6L,
         as_tibble_row(ix3(tab_S))),
  tibble(scenario = "Article 112 Diaspora District (Folded in)", seats = 128L, dia = 6L,
         as_tibble_row(ix3(tab_F))),
  tibble(scenario = "Proportional Diaspora District", seats = 128L, dia = 7L,
         as_tibble_row(ix3(tab_P))),
  tibble(scenario = "Best Alternative (No Diaspora District)", seats = 128L, dia = 0L,
         as_tibble_row(ix3(tab_ba)))) |>
  select(scenario, seats, dia, gal_geo, gal_conf, gal_cell, mal_geo, mal_conf, mal_cell)

# The findings this section rests on, pinned so a change to the data or the rules breaks here
# rather than silently rewriting the prose.
SQ_ <- 1L; S134_ <- 2L; S128_ <- 3L; P7_ <- 4L; BA_ <- 5L   # named so they stay readable
stopifnot(
  nrow(dia_scores) == 5L,
  # S134 - the ADD-ON phase - is worse than the status quo on all six measures
  all(dia_scores[S134_, IXM] > dia_scores[SQ_, IXM]),
  # On four of six it loses by MORE than the granularity advantage it enjoys, so those margins
  # are real; on geographic and cell Gallagher its deficit is INSIDE the gap, so those two are
  # ties and the argument must not be rested on them. Pinned exactly that way.
  sum(unlist(dia_scores[S134_, IXM] - dia_scores[SQ_, IXM]) > gran[IXM]) == 4L,
  all((unlist(dia_scores[S134_, IXM] - dia_scores[SQ_, IXM]) > gran[IXM])[
        c("mal_geo", "mal_conf", "mal_cell", "gal_conf")]),
  # the FOLD-IN beats the status quo on all three Gallagher levels
  all(dia_scores[S128_, c("gal_geo", "gal_conf", "gal_cell")] <=
      dia_scores[SQ_, c("gal_geo", "gal_conf", "gal_cell")]),
  # and leaves the confessional indices EXACTLY unchanged - neutral by construction
  all.equal(dia_scores$mal_conf[S128_], dia_scores$mal_conf[SQ_]),
  all.equal(dia_scores$gal_conf[S128_], dia_scores$gal_conf[SQ_]),
  # P7 is better than the status quo on every one of the six, and is the best of the DIASPORA
  # scenarios on cell - but NOT the best row in the table, because the benchmark beats it.
  all(dia_scores[P7_, IXM] < dia_scores[SQ_, IXM]),
  which.min(dia_scores$gal_cell[c(SQ_, S134_, S128_, P7_)]) == P7_,
  which.min(dia_scores$gal_cell) == BA_,
  # the benchmark moves 27 seats where the diaspora scenarios move 6 or 7
  sum(pmax(tab_ba$seats - tab_sq$seats, 0)) == 27L)

# Presentation follows Table \ref{tab:optima}: Gallagher at all three levels, then
# Loosemore-Hanby at cell level only, as a percentage and as a count of seats. The seat count uses
# each row's OWN chamber size, so the 134-seat row converts on 1.34 and the rest on 1.28 - the same
# rule as the master table. `dia_scores` keeps all six measures because the assertions above and
# Table \ref{tab:dia-grain} read them by name; only the display is narrowed.
dia_out <- dia_scores |>
  transmute(scenario, seats, dia, gal_geo, gal_conf, gal_cell,
            lh_pct = mal_cell, lh_seats = mal_cell * seats / 100)
stopifnot(abs(dia_out$lh_seats[S134_] - dia_out$lh_pct[S134_] * 1.34) < 1e-9,
          abs(dia_out$lh_seats[SQ_]   - dia_out$lh_pct[SQ_]   * 1.28) < 1e-9)

ltab(dia_out,
     caption = "Diaspora Voting: Status Quo vs. Diaspora District Alternatives",
     label = "dia-index",
     col.names = c("Scenario", "Seats", "Diaspora seats",
                   "District", "Confessional", "District x Confessional",
                   "%", "Seats"),
     header = c(" " = 3, "Gallagher" = 3, "Loosemore-Hanby" = 2),
     align = "lrrrrrrr", digits = c(0, 0, 0, 3, 3, 3, 2, 1), fit = TRUE)
```

### On comparing a 134-seat chamber with a 128-seat one

```{r dia-grain, comment = ""}
grain <- tibble(
  measure = c("SLH, geographic", "SLH, confessional", "SLH, cell",
              "Gallagher, geographic", "Gallagher, confessional", "Gallagher, cell"),
  floor128 = floors(128L)[IXM], floor134 = floors(134L)[IXM],
  advantage = gran[IXM],
  current = unlist(dia_scores[SQ_, IXM]), s134 = unlist(dia_scores[S134_, IXM])) |>
  mutate(margin = s134 - current,
         verdict = if_else(margin > advantage, "real", "inside the grain"))
stopifnot(sum(grain$verdict == "real") == 4L, all(grain$advantage > 0))

ltab(grain |> select(measure, floor128, floor134, advantage, margin, verdict),
     caption = paste0("Is S134's deficit larger than the advantage a bigger chamber gets for ",
       "free? \\emph{Floor} is the best value of that measure attainable by any allocation of ",
       "128 or 134 seats over the same sixteen-unit electorate, with no confessional or parity ",
       "constraint - largest remainder for SLH, greedy least-squares for Gallagher. ",
       "\\emph{Advantage} is the difference, the purely mechanical edge finer seats confer. ",
       "\\emph{Margin} is how much worse S134 is than the current table. On four measures the ",
       "margin is several times the advantage, so the deficit is real and understated; on ",
       "geographic and cell Gallagher it is smaller than the advantage, so those two should be ",
       "read as ties and no weight put on them."),
     label = "dia-grain",
     col.names = c("Measure", "Floor, 128", "Floor, 134", "Advantage to 134",
                   "S134 margin", "Verdict"),
     align = "lrrrrl", digits = c(0, 3, 3, 3, 3, 0))
```

## 6.4 Where the seats come from and go

```{r dia-grid, comment = ""}
# Seat change per cell against the STATUS QUO, plus the Gallagher slice of any group of cells
# before and after. Both sides share the same sixteen-unit grid, so the cells line up one to one;
# what differs is where the voters sit (the diaspora unit is empty in the status quo and holds its
# registrants afterwards) and the seat totals (128 under S128 and P7, 134 under S134). `v` is the
# baseline's voter column and `v1` the scenario's, so each side's deviation uses its own.
ORD <- c(unname(DISTRICT), DIA)                       # diaspora last, not alphabetically
DABBR_D <- c(DABBR, setNames("Dias.", DIA))           # local: DABBR itself is shared

dia_cells <- function(after) {
  stopifnot(identical(tab_sq$district, after$district), identical(tab_sq$faith, after$faith))
  V <- sum(tab_sq$v)
  tibble(district = factor(tab_sq$district, levels = ORD), faith = tab_sq$faith,
         v = tab_sq$v, v1 = after$v,
         s0 = tab_sq$seats, s1 = after$seats, d = after$seats - tab_sq$seats,
         dev0 = 100 * s0 / sum(tab_sq$seats) - 100 * v / V,
         dev1 = 100 * s1 / sum(after$seats) - 100 * v1 / V)
}
slice_delta <- function(g) sqrt(sum(g$dev1^2) / 2) - sqrt(sum(g$dev0^2) / 2)
d_gal <- function(cl, by) cl |> group_by(across(all_of(by))) |>
  group_modify(\(g, k) tibble(dgal = slice_delta(g))) |> ungroup() |> arrange(.data[[by]])

# The body holds whole seats and two margins hold Gallagher changes; `digits` applies down a
# whole column, so the table is assembled as text with each part formatted its own way.
as_seats <- function(x) if_else(is.na(x), "", formatC(x, format = "d"))
as_gal   <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3)

# `net_zero` says whether the chamber is the same size on both sides. Under P it is (seven
# seats leave the domestic table and seven arrive in the diaspora district) so the net-seats
# corner would necessarily read nought and is left blank, exactly as in section 5.6. Under S
# the chamber GROWS, so that corner carries the real total and is printed.
dia_grid_tab <- function(cl, net_zero) {
  f_seats <- cl |> summarise(net = sum(d), .by = faith)    |> arrange(faith)
  d_seats <- cl |> summarise(net = sum(d), .by = district) |> arrange(district)
  f_gal   <- d_gal(cl, "faith"); d_gal_ <- d_gal(cl, "district")
  stopifnot(sum(f_seats$net) == sum(d_seats$net))

  g <- cl |>
    mutate(cell = if_else(s0 == 0 & s1 == 0, NA_real_, as.numeric(d))) |>
    select(district, faith, cell) |> arrange(district) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = district, values_from = cell) |> arrange(faith) |>
    mutate(across(-faith, as_seats),
           Seats = as_seats(f_seats$net), Gallagher = as_gal(f_gal$dgal))

  mk_row <- function(label, vals, seats = "", gal = "")
    as_tibble(c(list(faith = label), as.list(vals), list(Seats = seats, Gallagher = gal)))
  g <- bind_rows(g,
    mk_row("Seats moved", setNames(as_seats(d_seats$net), as.character(d_seats$district)),
           seats = if (net_zero) "" else as_seats(sum(d_seats$net))),
    mk_row("Change in Gallagher",
           setNames(as_gal(d_gal_$dgal), as.character(d_gal_$district)),
           gal = as_gal(slice_delta(cl))))

  # Bold the cells that change, and both margin columns. The two foot rows are bolded by
  # bold_row, so they are FALSE here and \textbf never nests.
  m <- cl |> mutate(chg = d != 0) |> select(district, faith, chg) |> arrange(district) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = district, values_from = chg) |> arrange(faith)
  m <- cbind(as.matrix(m[, -1]), Seats = TRUE, Gallagher = TRUE)
  m[is.na(m)] <- FALSE
  list(tab = g, mask = rbind(m, rep(FALSE, ncol(m)), rep(FALSE, ncol(m))))
}

cl_P <- dia_cells(tab_P)
gp   <- dia_grid_tab(cl_P, net_zero = TRUE)

# The grid must reproduce the index table it sits next to, and the seat body must reproduce
# the carve-out table above it.
stopifnot(sum(abs(cl_P$d)) / 2 == 7, sum(cl_P$d) == 0,
          sum(cl_P$d != 0) == 12, sum(cl_P$d < 0) == 6, sum(cl_P$d > 0) == 6,
          abs(slice_delta(cl_P) -
                (ix3(tab_P)[["gal_cell"]] - ix3(tab_sq)[["gal_cell"]])) < 1e-9)

ltab(gp$tab,
     caption = "Seats gained and lost under Proportional Diaspora District",
     note = "Districts are abbreviated as in Table \\ref{tab:voters-per-seat}.",
     label = "dia-grid",
     col.names = c("Confession", DABBR_D[names(gp$tab)[2:17]], "Seats", "Gallagher"),
     align = paste0("l", strrep("r", 18)), fit = TRUE,
     bold_cells = gp$mask, bold_row = c(nrow(gp$tab) - 1L, nrow(gp$tab)))
```

```{r dia-grid-a112, comment = ""}
# The same machinery, for the two Article 112 scenarios. `net_zero` says whether the chamber is the
# same size on both sides: FALSE for the add-on, which grows to 134, so its net-seats corner carries
# the real total of +6 instead of being left blank.
cl_S <- dia_cells(tab_S)
cl_F <- dia_cells(tab_F)
gs   <- dia_grid_tab(cl_S, net_zero = FALSE)
gf   <- dia_grid_tab(cl_F, net_zero = TRUE)

stopifnot(all(cl_S$d[cl_S$district != DIA] == 0),   # the add-on touches no domestic seat
          sum(cl_S$d) == 6L,
          sum(cl_F$d) == 0L, sum(pmax(cl_F$d, 0)) == 6L,
          # each grid's corner is its own line in Table \ref{tab:dia-index}
          abs(slice_delta(cl_S) -
                (ix3(tab_S)[["gal_cell"]] - ix3(tab_sq)[["gal_cell"]])) < 1e-9,
          abs(slice_delta(cl_F) -
                (ix3(tab_F)[["gal_cell"]] - ix3(tab_sq)[["gal_cell"]])) < 1e-9)

ltab(gs$tab,
     caption = "Seats gained and lost under Article 112 Diaspora District (+6)",
     label = "dia-grid-a112",
     col.names = c("Confession", DABBR_D[names(gs$tab)[2:17]], "Seats", "Gallagher"),
     align = paste0("l", strrep("r", 18)), fit = TRUE,
     bold_cells = gs$mask, bold_row = c(nrow(gs$tab) - 1L, nrow(gs$tab)))

ltab(gf$tab,
     caption = "Seats gained and lost under Article 112 Diaspora District (Folded in)",
     note = "Districts are abbreviated as in Table \\ref{tab:voters-per-seat}.",
     label = "dia-grid-a112f",
     col.names = c("Confession", DABBR_D[names(gf$tab)[2:17]], "Seats", "Gallagher"),
     align = paste0("l", strrep("r", 18)), fit = TRUE,
     bold_cells = gf$mask, bold_row = c(nrow(gf$tab) - 1L, nrow(gf$tab)))
```

```{r dia-grid-S, comment = ""}
# The three-scenario comparison. `cl_S` and `cl_F` are built above.
# What is worth seeing side by side is the NET effect per confession,
# which is what decides the confessional index.
net_by_faith <- function(cl, nm) cl |>
  summarise(!!nm := as.integer(sum(d)), .by = faith)
gal_by_faith <- function(cl, nm) d_gal(cl, "faith") |> rename(!!nm := dgal)

S_out <- reduce(list(
  net_by_faith(cl_S, "n_S134"), net_by_faith(cl_F, "n_S128"),
  net_by_faith(cl_P, "n_P7"),
  gal_by_faith(cl_S, "g_S134"), gal_by_faith(cl_F, "g_S128"),
  gal_by_faith(cl_P, "g_P7")),
  \(a, b) left_join(a, b, by = "faith")) |> arrange(faith)

# S128 returns a seat from each named sect and hands the same sect one abroad, so every net is
# zero - the neutrality result of section 6.3, visible here as a column of noughts.
stopifnot(all(S_out$n_S128 == 0L))

S_tab <- S_out |>
  transmute(faith,
            n_S134 = as_seats(n_S134), n_S128 = as_seats(n_S128), n_P7 = as_seats(n_P7),
            g_S134 = as_gal(g_S134),   g_S128 = as_gal(g_S128),   g_P7 = as_gal(g_P7))
S_tab <- bind_rows(S_tab, tibble(
  faith  = "Total",
  n_S134 = as_seats(sum(cl_S$d)), n_S128 = as_seats(sum(cl_F$d)),
  n_P7   = as_seats(sum(cl_P$d)),
  g_S134 = as_gal(slice_delta(cl_S)), g_S128 = as_gal(slice_delta(cl_F)),
  g_P7   = as_gal(slice_delta(cl_P))))

ltab(S_tab,
     caption = paste0("Net seats and Gallagher slices by confession, all three scenarios, each ",
       "measured against the status quo and each row aggregating that confession's cells across ",
       "all sixteen districts. The Gallagher columns are that confession's slice of the CELL ",
       "index, ",
       "as in Table \\ref{tab:opt-grid}, not the confessional index. The S128 net column is ",
       "\\emph{all noughts}, which is the neutrality result of section 6.3 made visible: the ",
       "statute returns a seat from each named sect and awards the same sect one abroad, so no ",
       "confession's national total moves. The foot row gives seats added or moved - S134 grows ",
       "the chamber, so it totals six, while S128 and P7 are swaps and total nought - and the ",
       "change in the overall cell index. Gallagher slices combine in quadrature, so the foot ",
       "figures are not column sums. Negative Gallagher is an improvement."),
     label = "dia-grid-S",
     col.names = c("Confession", "S134", "S128", "P7", "S134", "S128", "P7"),
     align = "lrrrrrr", fit = TRUE, bold_row = nrow(S_tab))
```

## 6.5 All scenarios side by side

```{r optima-all, comment = ""}
# The diaspora scenarios in the same columns as section 5.5's seat tables. `moves` is the number of
# seats that change hands - the sum of the POSITIVE deltas against the status quo, which equals the
# usual sum(abs)/2 whenever the chamber size is held fixed, and correctly counts the six added seats
# under the Article 112 add-on row, where no domestic seat moves at all.
#
# `mal_seats` converts the Loosemore-Hanby percentage into a count of seats, so it must use each
# row's OWN chamber size: 134 for the add-on row, 128 everywhere else.
dia_row <- function(tab, label) {
  z <- ix3(tab); d <- tab$seats - tab_sq$seats
  tibble(table = label,
         moves = sum(pmax(d, 0)),
         districts = n_distinct(tab$district[d != 0]),
         gal_geo = z[["gal_geo"]], gal_conf = z[["gal_conf"]], gal_cell = z[["gal_cell"]],
         mal_cell = z[["mal_cell"]], mal_seats = z[["mal_cell"]] * sum(tab$seats) / 100)
}

# The two scorers must agree on the status quo, or the rows are not on a common footing. `ix_cv`
# works over 15 districts and 180 cells, `ix3` over 16 and 192 with twelve of them empty.
stopifnot(all.equal(unname(ix3(tab_sq)[c("gal_geo", "gal_conf", "gal_cell", "mal_cell")]),
                    unname(z0[c("gal_geo", "gal_conf", "gal_cell", "mal_cell")]),
                    tolerance = 1e-9))

optab_all <- bind_rows(
  optab,
  dia_row(tab_S, "Article 112 Diaspora District (+6 seats)"),
  dia_row(tab_F, "Article 112 Diaspora District (Folded in)"),
  dia_row(tab_P, "Proportional Diaspora District"))

stopifnot(nrow(optab_all) == 8L,
          identical(optab_all$table[2], "Proportional Ideal (without Taif Agreement)"),
          # the add-on row adds six seats and moves none; the fold-in row moves six
          optab_all$moves[6] == 6L, optab_all$districts[6] == 1L,
          optab_all$moves[7] == 6L, optab_all$moves[8] == 7L,
          # and its seat count is taken on 134, not 128
          abs(optab_all$mal_seats[6] - optab_all$mal_cell[6] * 1.34) < 1e-9,
          abs(optab_all$mal_seats[1] - optab_all$mal_cell[1] * 1.28) < 1e-9)

ltab(optab_all,
     caption = "Malapportionment of Status Quo vs. Proposed Alternative Allocations",
     label = "optima",
     col.names = c("", "Seat moves", "Districts touched",
                   "District", "Confessional", "District x Confessional",
                   "%", "Seats"),
     header = c(" " = 3, "Gallagher Index" = 3, "Loosemore-Hanby Index" = 2),
     digits = c(0, 0, 0, 3, 3, 3, 2, 1), fit = TRUE)
```

# 7. Appendix

## 7.1 Seats gained and lost without the 64--64 rule

```{r opt-grid-free, comment = ""}
# The same grid section 5.6 builds for the parity-respecting optimum, for the unconstrained one.
# Written as a function rather than inline so the two are demonstrably the same computation; the
# 5.6 chunk is left exactly as it is, since it is already correct and in the paper.
change_grid <- function(new_seats) {
  g <- cv |> mutate(new = new_seats, d = new - s0,
                    dev0 = 100 * s0  / sum(s0)  - 100 * v / sum(cv$v),
                    dev1 = 100 * new / sum(new) - 100 * v / sum(cv$v))
  sd_    <- function(x) sqrt(sum(x$dev1^2) / 2) - sqrt(sum(x$dev0^2) / 2)
  by_gal <- function(by) g |> group_by(across(all_of(by))) |>
    group_modify(\(x, k) tibble(dgal = sd_(x))) |> ungroup() |> arrange(.data[[by]])

  f_seats <- g |> summarise(net = sum(d), .by = vfaith)   |> arrange(vfaith)
  d_seats <- g |> summarise(net = sum(d), .by = district) |> arrange(district)
  stopifnot(sum(f_seats$net) == 0, sum(d_seats$net) == 0)          # a swap on both axes

  tab <- g |>
    mutate(cell = if_else(s0 == 0 & new == 0, NA_real_, as.numeric(d))) |>
    select(district, vfaith, cell) |> arrange(district) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = district, values_from = cell) |> arrange(vfaith) |>
    mutate(across(-vfaith, as_seats),
           Seats = as_seats(f_seats$net), Gallagher = as_gal(by_gal("vfaith")$dgal))

  mk <- function(label, vals, gal = "")
    as_tibble(c(list(vfaith = label), as.list(vals), list(Seats = "", Gallagher = gal)))
  tab <- bind_rows(tab,
    mk("Seats moved", setNames(as_seats(d_seats$net), d_seats$district)),
    mk("Change in Gallagher", setNames(as_gal(by_gal("district")$dgal), d_seats$district),
       gal = as_gal(sd_(g))))

  m <- g |> mutate(chg = d != 0) |> select(district, vfaith, chg) |> arrange(district) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = district, values_from = chg) |> arrange(vfaith)
  m <- cbind(as.matrix(m[, -1]), Seats = TRUE, Gallagher = TRUE)
  m[is.na(m)] <- FALSE
  list(tab = tab, mask = rbind(m, rep(FALSE, ncol(m)), rep(FALSE, ncol(m))),
       moves = sum(abs(g$d)) / 2, cells = sum(g$d != 0), corner = sd_(g))
}

gfree <- change_grid(free_cell)

# The grid must reproduce section 5.5's own figures for this table, and the parity split it implies.
stopifnot(gfree$moves == 27, gfree$cells == 39,
          abs(gfree$corner - (ix_cv(free_cell)[["gal_cell"]] - z0[["gal_cell"]])) < 1e-9,
          sum(free_cell[cv$bloc == "Christian"]) == 41L,
          sum(free_cell[cv$bloc == "Muslim"])    == 87L)

ltab(gfree$tab,
     caption = paste0("Seats gained and lost from status quo to proportional ideal with 128 seats ",
                      "(no Taif agreement restriction). Districts are abbreviated as in Table ",
                      "\\ref{tab:voters-per-seat}."),
     label = "opt-grid-free",
     col.names = c("Confession", DABBR[names(gfree$tab)[2:16]], "Seats", "Gallagher"),
     align = paste0("l", strrep("r", 17)), fit = TRUE,
     bold_cells = gfree$mask, bold_row = c(nrow(gfree$tab) - 1L, nrow(gfree$tab)))
```
